chapter: Tiny Bradshaw, Teddy Hill and Europe
title: Why Procope left Teddy Hill: the fired singer and the Toscanini attitude
summary: Hill fired a girl singer who stopped the show with Loch Lomond in Philadelphia and, back from Europe, turned down an Apollo date; Procope left, saying Hill aimed too high.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: singer with the band and this was during the time Maxine Sullivan came up with "Loch Lomond". "Loch Lomond" was a big hit. Any band that was playing at that time had to play "Loch Lomond." So Teddy's band -- we were playing this theater in Philadelphia, I think it was the Lincoln Theater, and so this girl sang "Loch Lomond" and locked up the show. They wouldn't let us off the stage, just from her singing "Loch Lomond". And do you know Teddy fired her. You wouldn't believe it. But that's the type of man he was. And I left him after we came back from Europe. After we came back from Europe he thought he was Toscanini, you know? And of course I resented that, and Shiman -- we could have gone to work that following week after we got off the boat, in he Apollo. He turned it down. See, that's the type of person he was. And I said, "What did you turn it down for?" So this is during the time I joined Kirby.
I went down to -- we were off. We were off, Teddy's band. We didn't work for maybe a month after we got back from Europe. Which was a crazy, silly thing to do.
